body.v: The notes are in the shared folder as usual, no sign-in needed. I put the actions at the top.
Tell me if I missed anything and we can go through it on the phone.
You wrote on Wednesday: "The notes are final, I will share them after the call."

hotspots.explain: The address is Jonas's and the thread is real. Alone, that proves little, but here the rest matches.
Same shared folder as always, and no sign-in. Nothing is asked of you.
He offers a phone call, a channel you can use any time.
It quotes your own words, which fits a real conversation.

who.prompt: Who is really writing to you? Look at the address, not just the name.
who.answer: Jonas, most likely: a real thread, the usual folder and an offer to talk by phone.

emotion.prompt: What feeling is this email trying to create?
emotion.answer: None. It is a friendly, everyday message.
choices: None: it is an everyday message

ask.prompt: What exactly does it want you to do?
ask.answer: Nothing. The notes are in the usual folder. There is no link and no new sign-in.
choices: Nothing: the notes are in the usual place
Sign in again through a link

verify.prompt: How can you check through a channel you control?
verify.answer: Look in the shared folder yourself. If anything bothers you, call Jonas on the number you already have.
choices: Open the shared folder yourself, or call Jonas
Reply to ask if it is really him

actions.label: Open the shared folder yourself and read the notes
actions.consequence: The notes are there, as Jonas said.

actions.label: Call Jonas to talk through the notes
actions.consequence: He confirms. A short call is never wasted.

actions.label: Sign in again somewhere, just in case
actions.consequence: Nothing asked for it. Never type a login when no real request needs it.

attacker_reveal: This one is real, dear. It is almost a twin of the 'sign in again' email, but this one asks for nothing and points to the usual folder. At this level, ask what is being requested.
